verses.1:1: The beginning of the gospel of Jesus Christ, Son of God.
verses.1:2: Just as it has been written in Isaiah the prophet: "Look, I am sending My messenger before Your face, who will prepare Your way;
verses.1:3: a voice of one crying out in the wilderness: 'Make ready the way of the Lord; make His paths straight,'"
verses.1:4: John appeared, the one baptizing in the wilderness and proclaiming a baptism of repentance for the forgiveness of sins.
verses.1:5: And all the Judean countryside and all the people of Jerusalem were going out to him, and they were being baptized by him in the Jordan River, confessing their sins.
verses.1:6: And John was clothed with camel's hair and a leather belt around his waist, and he was eating locusts and wild honey.
verses.1:7: And he was proclaiming, saying, "After me comes the One stronger than I, the strap of whose sandals I am not worthy to stoop down and untie.
verses.1:8: I baptized you with water, but He will baptize you in the Holy Spirit."
verses.1:9: And it happened in those days that Jesus came from Nazareth of Galilee and was baptized in the Jordan by John.
verses.1:10: And immediately, coming up out of the water, He saw the heavens being torn open and the Spirit descending like a dove upon Him;
verses.1:11: and a voice came out of the heavens: "You are My Son, the Beloved; in You I delight."
verses.1:12: And immediately the Spirit drove Him out into the wilderness.
verses.1:13: And He was in the wilderness forty days, being tempted by Satan, and He was with the wild animals, and the angels were serving Him.
verses.1:14: And after John was handed over, Jesus came into Galilee, proclaiming the gospel of God
verses.1:15: and saying, "The appointed time has been fulfilled, and the kingdom of God has drawn near; repent and believe in the gospel."
verses.1:16: And as He was passing along beside the Sea of Galilee, He saw Simon and Andrew, the brother of Simon, casting a net in the sea, for they were fishermen.
verses.1:17: And Jesus said to them, "Come after Me, and I will make you become fishers of people."
verses.1:18: And immediately, leaving the nets, they followed Him.
verses.1:19: And going on a little farther, He saw James the son of Zebedee and John his brother, and them also in the boat mending the nets,
verses.1:20: and immediately He called them. And leaving their father Zebedee in the boat with the hired men, they went away after Him.
verses.1:21: And they entered into Capernaum. And immediately on the Sabbath, having gone into the synagogue, He was teaching.
verses.1:22: And they were astonished at His teaching, for He was teaching them as one having authority, and not as the scribes.
verses.1:23: And immediately there was in their synagogue a man with an unclean spirit, and he cried out,
verses.1:24: saying, "What is there between us and You, Jesus the Nazarene? Have You come to destroy us? I know who You are—the Holy One of God!"
verses.1:25: And Jesus rebuked it, saying, "Be silenced and come out of him!"
verses.1:26: And the unclean spirit, convulsing him and crying out with a loud voice, came out of him.
verses.1:27: And they were all amazed, so that they questioned among themselves, saying, "What is this? A new teaching! With authority He commands even the unclean spirits, and they obey Him."
verses.1:28: And immediately the report about Him went out everywhere into the whole surrounding region of Galilee.
verses.1:29: And immediately, having come out of the synagogue, they went into the house of Simon and Andrew, with James and John.
verses.1:30: Now Simon's mother-in-law was lying down with a fever, and immediately they told Him about her.
verses.1:31: And approaching her, He raised her up, taking hold of her hand; and the fever left her, and she began serving them.
verses.1:32: Now when evening came, when the sun set, they were bringing to Him all those who were ill and those who were demon-possessed;
verses.1:33: and the whole city was gathered together at the door.
verses.1:34: And He healed many who were ill with various diseases, and He drove out many demons; and He would not permit the demons to speak, because they knew Him.
verses.1:35: And very early in the morning, while it was still night, rising up, He went out and departed to a desolate place, and there He was praying.
verses.1:36: And Simon and those with him searched for Him,
verses.1:37: and they found Him and said to Him, "Everyone is looking for You."
verses.1:38: And He said to them, "Let us go elsewhere into the neighboring towns, so that I may proclaim there also, for this is why I came out."
verses.1:39: And He went proclaiming in their synagogues throughout all Galilee and driving out the demons.
verses.1:40: And a leper came to Him, imploring Him and kneeling down, saying to Him, "If You are willing, You are able to cleanse me."
verses.1:41: And moved with compassion, stretching out His hand, He touched him and said to him, "I am willing; be cleansed."
verses.1:42: And immediately the leprosy departed from him, and he was cleansed.
verses.1:43: And sternly warning him, He immediately sent him away,
verses.1:44: and said to him, "See that you say nothing to anyone, but go, show yourself to the priest and offer for your cleansing what Moses commanded, as a testimony to them."
verses.1:45: But having gone out, he began to proclaim widely and to spread the word, so that He was no longer able to enter openly into a city, but remained outside in desolate places; and they were coming to Him from everywhere.
verses.2:1: And when He entered Capernaum again after some days, it was heard that He was at home.
verses.2:2: And many gathered together so that there was no longer room, not even around the door, and He was speaking the word to them.
verses.2:3: And they came bringing to Him a paralyzed man, carried by four men.
verses.2:4: And not being able to bring him to Him because of the crowd, they removed the roof where He was; and after digging through it, they lowered the mat on which the paralyzed man was lying.
verses.2:5: And seeing their faith, Jesus said to the paralyzed man, "Child, your sins are forgiven."
verses.2:6: Now some of the scribes were sitting there and reasoning in their hearts,
verses.2:7: "Why does this man speak like this? He is blaspheming! Who can forgive sins except God alone?"
verses.2:8: And immediately Jesus, perceiving in His spirit that they were reasoning this way within themselves, said to them, "Why are you reasoning about these things in your hearts?
verses.2:9: Which is easier, to say to the paralyzed man, 'Your sins are forgiven,' or to say, 'Get up and pick up your mat and walk'?
verses.2:10: But so that you may know that the Son of Man has authority on earth to forgive sins"—He said to the paralyzed man,
verses.2:11: "I say to you, get up, pick up your mat, and go to your home."
verses.2:12: And he got up, and immediately picking up the mat, he went out in front of everyone, so that all were amazed and glorified God, saying, "We have never seen anything like this."
verses.2:13: And He went out again beside the sea; and the entire crowd was coming to Him, and He was teaching them.
verses.2:14: And as He passed by, He saw Levi the son of Alphaeus sitting at the tax booth, and He said to him, "Follow Me." And rising up, he followed Him.
verses.2:15: And it came about that He was reclining at table in his house, and many tax collectors and sinners were reclining with Jesus and His disciples, for there were many, and they were following Him.
verses.2:16: And when the scribes of the Pharisees saw that He was eating with the sinners and tax collectors, they were saying to His disciples, "Why does He eat with the tax collectors and sinners?"
verses.2:17: And hearing this, Jesus said to them, "Those who are healthy have no need of a physician, but those who are ill; I did not come to call the righteous, but sinners."
verses.2:18: And John's disciples and the Pharisees were fasting. And they came and said to Him, "Why do the disciples of John and the disciples of the Pharisees fast, yet Your disciples do not fast?"
verses.2:19: And Jesus said to them, "Can the sons of the bridal chamber fast while the bridegroom is with them? As long as they have the bridegroom with them, they cannot fast.
verses.2:20: Yet days will come when the bridegroom is taken away from them, and then they will fast in that day.
verses.2:21: No one sews a patch of unshrunk cloth onto an old garment; otherwise, the patch pulls away from it, the new from the old, and a worse tear occurs.
verses.2:22: And no one pours new wine into old wineskins; otherwise, the wine will burst the wineskins, and the wine is lost along with the skins. Rather, new wine belongs in fresh wineskins."
verses.2:23: And it happened that He was passing through the grainfields on the Sabbath, and His disciples began to make their way while plucking the heads of grain.
verses.2:24: And the Pharisees were saying to Him, "Look, why are they doing on the Sabbath what is not lawful?"
verses.2:25: And He said to them, "Have you never read what David did when he was in need and grew hungry, he and those who were with him,
verses.2:26: how he entered the house of God in the time of Abiathar the high priest and ate the loaves of presentation, which it is not lawful for anyone to eat except the priests, and gave some also to those who were with him?"
verses.2:27: And He was saying to them, "The Sabbath came into being for the sake of man, and not man for the sake of the Sabbath;
verses.2:28: so the Son of Man is Lord even of the Sabbath."
verses.3:1: And He entered a synagogue again, and a man was there who had a withered hand.
verses.3:2: And they were watching Him closely to see whether He would heal him on the Sabbath, so that they might accuse Him.
verses.3:3: And He said to the man who had the withered hand, "Rise and stand in the middle."
verses.3:4: And He said to them, "Is it lawful on the Sabbath to do good or to do harm, to save a life or to kill?" But they remained silent.
verses.3:5: And looking around at them with anger, grieved at the hardness of their heart, He said to the man, "Stretch out your hand." And he stretched it out, and his hand was restored.
verses.3:6: And going out immediately, the Pharisees began taking counsel with the Herodians against Him, as to how they might destroy Him.
verses.3:7: And Jesus withdrew with His disciples to the sea; and a great multitude from Galilee followed, and from Judea,
verses.3:8: and from Jerusalem, and from Idumea, and from beyond the Jordan, and around Tyre and Sidon, a great multitude, hearing all that He was doing, came to Him.
verses.3:9: And He told His disciples that a small boat should be kept ready for Him because of the crowd, so that they would not crush Him;
verses.3:10: for He had healed many, so that all who had afflictions were pressing in upon Him in order to touch Him.
verses.3:11: And whenever the unclean spirits saw Him, they would fall down before Him and cry out, saying, "You are the Son of God."
verses.3:12: And He sternly warned them not to make Him known.
verses.3:13: And He went up on the mountain and summoned those whom He Himself wanted, and they came to Him.
verses.3:14: And He appointed twelve, whom He also named apostles, so that they might be with Him and so that He might send them out to preach,
verses.3:15: and to have authority to drive out the demons;
verses.3:16: and He appointed the twelve: and to Simon He gave the name Peter,
verses.3:17: and James the son of Zebedee and John the brother of James (and He gave them the name Boanerges, which is Sons of Thunder),
verses.3:18: and Andrew, and Philip, and Bartholomew, and Matthew, and Thomas, and James the son of Alphaeus, and Thaddaeus, and Simon the Cananaean,
verses.3:19: and Judas Iscariot, who also betrayed Him.
verses.3:20: And He came home; and the crowd gathered together again, so that they were not even able to eat bread.
verses.3:21: And when His own people heard of this, they went out to take hold of Him, for they were saying, "He is out of His mind."
verses.3:22: And the scribes who had come down from Jerusalem were saying, "He has Beelzebul," and, "By the ruler of the demons He drives out the demons."
verses.3:23: And summoning them, He began speaking to them in parables: "How can Satan drive out Satan?
verses.3:24: And if a kingdom is divided against itself, that kingdom cannot stand;
verses.3:25: and if a house is divided against itself, that house will not be able to stand;
verses.3:26: and if Satan has risen against himself and been divided, he cannot stand, but has an end.
verses.3:27: However, no one can go into the house of the strong man and plunder his belongings unless he first binds the strong man, and then he will plunder his house.
verses.3:28: Truly I say to you, all things will be forgiven the sons of men—the sins and whatever blasphemies they utter;
verses.3:29: but whoever blasphemes against the Holy Spirit has no forgiveness forever, rather he is guilty of an eternal sin."
verses.3:30: For they were saying, "He has an unclean spirit."
verses.3:31: And His mother and His brothers came, and standing outside they sent to Him, calling for Him.
verses.3:32: And a crowd was sitting around Him, and they said to Him, "Look, Your mother and Your brothers are outside looking for You."
verses.3:33: And answering them, He said, "Who are My mother and My brothers?"
verses.3:34: And looking around at those sitting in a circle around Him, He said, "Here are My mother and My brothers!
verses.3:35: For whoever does the will of God, this one is My brother and sister and mother."
verses.4:1: And again He began to teach beside the sea. And a very large crowd gathered to Him, so that He got into a boat and sat on the sea, and the whole crowd was by the sea on the land.
verses.4:2: And He was teaching them many things in parables, and He was saying to them in His teaching:
verses.4:3: "Listen! Look, the sower went out to sow.
verses.4:4: And it happened as he was sowing that some fell beside the path, and the birds came and devoured it.
verses.4:5: And other seed fell on the rocky ground where it did not have much soil, and immediately it sprang up because it had no depth of soil;
verses.4:6: and when the sun rose, it was scorched, and because it had no root, it withered away.
verses.4:7: And other seed fell among the thorns, and the thorns grew up and choked it, and it yielded no fruit.
verses.4:8: And other seeds fell into the good soil, and they yielded fruit, growing up and increasing, and bore thirtyfold, and sixtyfold, and a hundredfold."
verses.4:9: And He was saying, "The one who has ears to hear, let him hear."
verses.4:10: And when He was alone, those around Him, together with the twelve, were asking Him about the parables.
verses.4:11: And He was saying to them, "To you the mystery of the kingdom of God has been given, but to those outside, all things come in parables,
verses.4:12: so that seeing they may see and not perceive, and hearing they may hear and not understand, otherwise they might turn back and be forgiven."
verses.4:13: And He said to them, "Do you not understand this parable? And how will you comprehend all the parables?
verses.4:15: Now these are the ones beside the path where the word is sown; and when they hear, Satan immediately comes and takes away the word that has been sown in them.
verses.4:16: And in the same way, these are the ones sown on the rocky places, who, when they hear the word, immediately receive it with joy,
verses.4:17: and they have no root in themselves, but are temporary; then, when affliction or persecution arises because of the word, immediately they stumble.
verses.4:18: And others are the ones sown among the thorns; these are the ones who heard the word,
verses.4:19: and the anxieties of the age, and the deceitfulness of wealth, and the desires for other things enter in and choke the word, and it becomes unfruitful.
verses.4:20: And those are the ones sown on the good soil, who hear the word and welcome it and bear fruit—thirtyfold, and sixtyfold, and a hundredfold."
verses.4:21: And He was saying to them, "A lamp is not brought in to be placed under a measuring basket or under a bed, is it? Is it not to be placed on a lampstand?
verses.4:22: For nothing is hidden except so that it may be revealed, nor has anything become secret except so that it may come into the open.
verses.4:23: If anyone has ears to hear, let him hear."
verses.4:24: And He was saying to them, "Watch closely what you hear. By the measure with which you measure, it will be measured to you, and more will be added to you.
verses.4:25: For whoever has, to him it will be given; and whoever does not have, even what he has will be taken away from him."
verses.4:26: And He was saying, "The kingdom of God is like this: as if a man scatters seed on the soil,
verses.4:27: and sleeps and gets up night and day, and the seed sprouts and grows—how, he himself does not know.
verses.4:28: All by itself the soil bears fruit: first the blade, then the head, then the full grain in the head.
verses.4:29: And when the fruit is ripe, immediately he sends forth the sickle, because the harvest has arrived."
verses.4:30: And He was saying, "How shall we compare the kingdom of God, or in what parable shall we present it?
verses.4:31: It is like a mustard seed, which, when it is sown upon the soil, though smaller than all the seeds on the earth—
verses.4:32: yet when it is sown, it grows up and becomes larger than all the garden plants and puts out large branches, so that the birds of the sky are able to nest under its shade."
verses.4:33: And with many such parables He was speaking the word to them, as they were able to hear it;
verses.4:34: and without a parable He was not speaking to them, yet in private He was explaining everything to His own disciples.
verses.4:35: And on that day, when evening had come, He said to them, "Let us cross over to the other side."
verses.4:36: And leaving the crowd behind, they took Him along, just as He was, in the boat; and other boats were with Him.
verses.4:37: And a fierce squall of wind arose, and the waves were breaking into the boat, so that the boat was already filling up.
verses.4:38: And He Himself was in the stern, sleeping on the cushion; and they woke Him and said to Him, "Teacher, do You not care that we are perishing?"
verses.4:39: And waking up, He rebuked the wind and said to the sea, "Be silent! Be still!" And the wind died down, and there was a great calm.
verses.4:40: And He said to them, "Why are you fearful? Do you not yet have faith?"
verses.4:41: And they were filled with great fear, and they were saying to one another, "Who indeed is this, that even the wind and the sea obey Him?"
verses.5:1: And they came to the other side of the sea, into the region of the Gerasenes.
verses.5:2: And when He came out of the boat, immediately a man from the tombs with an unclean spirit met Him,
verses.5:3: who had his dwelling among the tombs. And no one was any longer able to bind him, not even with a chain,
verses.5:4: because he had often been bound with shackles and chains, and the chains had been torn apart by him and the shackles shattered; and no one had the strength to subdue him.
verses.5:5: And continually, night and day, among the tombs and in the mountains, he was crying out and gashing himself with stones.
verses.5:6: And seeing Jesus from a distance, he ran and bowed down before Him,
verses.5:7: and crying out with a loud voice, he said, "What is between me and You, Jesus, Son of the Most High God? I charge You by God, do not torment me!"
verses.5:8: For He was saying to him, "Come out of the man, unclean spirit!"
verses.5:9: And He asked him, "What is your name?" And he said to Him, "Legion is my name, because we are many."
verses.5:10: And he kept begging Him earnestly not to send them out of the region.
verses.5:11: Now a large herd of pigs was feeding there near the mountain.
verses.5:12: And they begged Him, saying, "Send us into the pigs, so that we may enter them."
verses.5:13: And He gave them permission. And the unclean spirits came out and entered the pigs, and the herd rushed down the steep bank into the sea, about two thousand of them, and they were drowning in the sea.
verses.5:14: And those who were herding them fled and reported it in the city and in the countryside, and people came out to see what it was that had happened.
verses.5:15: And they came to Jesus and saw the demon-possessed man sitting there, clothed and in his right mind, the one who had had the legion, and they became afraid.
verses.5:16: And those who had seen it recounted to them how it had happened to the demon-possessed man, and about the pigs.
verses.5:17: And they began to beg Him to depart from their territory.
verses.5:18: And as He was getting into the boat, the man who had been demon-possessed was begging Him that he might be with Him.
verses.5:19: And He did not permit him, but said to him, "Go to your house, to your own people, and report to them how much the Lord has done for you and how He has had mercy on you."
verses.5:20: And he departed and began to proclaim in the Decapolis how much Jesus had done for him, and everyone was marveling.
verses.5:21: And when Jesus had crossed over again in the boat to the other side, a large crowd gathered around Him, and He was beside the sea.
verses.5:22: And one of the synagogue rulers, named Jairus, came, and seeing Him, fell at His feet
verses.5:23: and begged Him earnestly, saying, "My little daughter is at the point of death. Come and lay Your hands on her, so that she may be made well and live."
verses.5:24: And He went with him. And a large crowd was following Him and pressing in on Him.
verses.5:25: And a woman who had a flow of blood for twelve years,
verses.5:26: and had suffered much under many physicians and spent all that she had, and was not helped at all, but rather had grown worse,
verses.5:27: having heard the things about Jesus, came up from behind in the crowd and touched His garment.
verses.5:28: For she was saying, "If I touch even His garments, I will be made well."
verses.5:29: And immediately the source of her blood dried up, and she knew in her body that she had been healed of the affliction.
verses.5:30: And immediately Jesus, perceiving in Himself that power had gone out from Him, turned around in the crowd and said, "Who touched My garments?"
verses.5:31: And His disciples were saying to Him, "You see the crowd pressing in on You, and You say, 'Who touched Me?'"
verses.5:32: And He kept looking around to see the woman who had done this.
verses.5:33: But the woman, frightened and trembling, knowing what had happened to her, came and fell down before Him and told Him the whole truth.
verses.5:34: And He said to her, "Daughter, your faith has made you well. Go in peace, and be cured of your affliction."
verses.5:35: While He was still speaking, some came from the synagogue ruler's house, saying, "Your daughter has died. Why trouble the Teacher any further?"
verses.5:36: But Jesus, disregarding the word being spoken, said to the synagogue ruler, "Do not be afraid; only believe."
verses.5:37: And He did not permit anyone to accompany Him except Peter and James and John, the brother of James.
verses.5:38: And they came to the house of the synagogue ruler, and He saw a commotion, and people weeping and wailing loudly.
verses.5:39: And having entered, He said to them, "Why are you making a commotion and weeping? The child has not died, but is sleeping."
verses.5:40: And they were laughing at Him. But having put everyone outside, He took along the father of the child and the mother and those with Him, and entered where the child was.
verses.5:41: And taking hold of the child's hand, He said to her, "Talitha koum!" which translated means, "Little girl, I say to you, rise."
verses.5:42: And immediately the little girl rose and began walking around, for she was twelve years old. And immediately they were astounded with great astonishment.
verses.5:43: And He strictly charged them that no one should know this, and He said to give her something to eat.
verses.6:1: And He departed from there and came to His hometown, and His disciples followed Him.
verses.6:2: And when the Sabbath came, He began to teach in the synagogue; and the many who heard were astonished, saying, "Where did this man get these things? And what is this wisdom that has been given to Him, and such deeds of power happening through His hands?
verses.6:3: Is this not the carpenter, the son of Mary and brother of James and Joses and Judas and Simon? And are not His sisters here with us?" And they took offense at Him.
verses.6:4: And Jesus was saying to them, "No prophet is without honor except in his hometown, among his relatives, and in his own household."
verses.6:5: And He could not perform any deed of power there, except that He laid His hands on a few sick people and healed them.
verses.6:6: And He marveled because of their unbelief. And He went around the surrounding villages teaching.
verses.6:7: And He summoned the twelve and began to send them out two by two, and He was giving them authority over the unclean spirits,
verses.6:8: and He instructed them to take nothing for the journey except a staff alone: no bread, no bag, no copper money in their belt,
verses.6:9: but to wear sandals, and not to put on two tunics.
verses.6:10: And He said to them, "Wherever you enter a house, stay there until you depart from there.
verses.6:11: And whatever place does not receive you and they do not listen to you, as you go out from there, shake off the dust beneath your feet as a testimony to them."
verses.6:12: And they went out and proclaimed that people should repent,
verses.6:13: and they were casting out many demons, and were anointing many sick people with oil and healing them.
verses.6:14: And King Herod heard of it, for His name had become well known; and people were saying, "John the Baptizer has been raised from the dead, and because of this these powers are at work in him."
verses.6:15: But others were saying, "He is Elijah." And others were saying, "A prophet, like one of the prophets."
verses.6:16: But when Herod heard of it, he was saying, "John, whom I beheaded, he has been raised."
verses.6:17: For Herod himself had sent and seized John and bound him in prison on account of Herodias, the wife of his brother Philip, because he had married her.
verses.6:18: For John had been saying to Herod, "It is not lawful for you to have your brother's wife."
verses.6:19: And Herodias held a grudge against him and wanted to put him to death, and she was not able to;
verses.6:20: for Herod feared John, knowing him to be a righteous and holy man, and he kept him safe; and when he heard him, he was greatly perplexed, yet he listened to him gladly.
verses.6:21: And an opportune day arrived when Herod, on his birthday, gave a banquet for his nobles and the military commanders and the leading men of Galilee;
verses.6:22: and when his daughter Herodias came in and danced, she pleased Herod and those reclining at table with him. And the king said to the girl, "Ask me for whatever you wish, and I will give it to you."
verses.6:23: And he swore to her, "Whatever you ask of me, I will give to you, up to half of my kingdom."
verses.6:24: And she went out and said to her mother, "What should I ask for?" And she said, "The head of John the Baptizer."
verses.6:25: And immediately she came in with haste to the king and made her request, saying, "I want you to give me at once on a platter the head of John the Baptist."
verses.6:26: And though the king became deeply grieved, because of his oaths and those reclining at table with him, he did not want to refuse her.
verses.6:27: And immediately the king sent an executioner and commanded him to bring his head. And he went and beheaded him in the prison,
verses.6:28: and brought his head on a platter and gave it to the girl, and the girl gave it to her mother.
verses.6:29: And when his disciples heard about it, they came and took away his body and laid it in a tomb.
verses.6:30: And the apostles gathered together to Jesus and reported to Him all that they had done and all that they had taught.
verses.6:31: And He said to them, "Come away by yourselves to a desolate place and rest a little while." For there were many coming and going, and they did not even have an opportunity to eat.
verses.6:32: And they went away in the boat to a desolate place by themselves.
verses.6:33: And many saw them going and recognized them, and they ran there together on foot from all the cities and arrived ahead of them.
verses.6:34: And when He stepped ashore, He saw a large crowd, and He felt compassion for them, because they were like sheep not having a shepherd; and He began to teach them many things.
verses.6:35: And when the hour had already grown late, His disciples came to Him and were saying, "This place is desolate, and the hour is already late;
verses.6:36: send them away so that they may go into the surrounding countryside and villages and buy themselves something to eat."
verses.6:37: But He answered and said to them, "You yourselves give them something to eat." And they said to Him, "Should we go and buy two hundred denarii worth of bread and give it to them to eat?"
verses.6:38: And He said to them, "How many loaves do you have? Go and see." And when they found out, they said, "Five, and two fish."
verses.6:39: And He commanded them to have everyone recline in groups on the green grass.
verses.6:40: And they reclined in orderly groups, by hundreds and by fifties.
verses.6:41: And taking the five loaves and the two fish, looking up to heaven, He spoke a blessing and broke the loaves and was giving them to His disciples to set before them, and He divided the two fish among them all.
verses.6:42: And they all ate and were satisfied;
verses.6:43: and they picked up twelve basketfuls of the broken pieces and also from the fish.
verses.6:44: And those who ate the loaves were five thousand men.
verses.6:45: And immediately He compelled His disciples to board the boat and go ahead to the other side, toward Bethsaida, while He Himself dismissed the crowd.
verses.6:46: And after taking leave of them, He went away to the mountain to pray.
verses.6:47: And when evening had come, the boat was in the middle of the sea, and He was alone on the land.
verses.6:48: And seeing them straining at rowing, for the wind was against them, around the fourth watch of the night He came to them, walking on the sea; and He intended to pass by them.
verses.6:49: But when they saw Him walking on the sea, they thought that it was a ghost, and they cried out;
verses.6:50: for they all saw Him and were terrified. But immediately He spoke with them and said to them, "Take courage; it is I. Do not be afraid."
verses.6:51: And He got up into the boat with them, and the wind died down. And they were utterly amazed within themselves,
verses.6:52: for they had not understood concerning the loaves, but their heart was hardened.
verses.6:53: And when they had crossed over to the land, they came to Gennesaret and moored to the shore.
verses.6:54: And when they came out of the boat, people immediately recognized Him
verses.6:55: and ran around that entire region and began to carry around on mats those who were ill, to wherever they heard He was.
verses.6:56: And wherever He entered into villages or cities or countryside, they were laying those who were sick in the marketplaces and pleading with Him that they might touch even the fringe of His garment; and as many as touched it were made well.
verses.7:1: And the Pharisees and some of the scribes who had come from Jerusalem gathered to Him,
verses.7:2: and saw that some of His disciples were eating bread with defiled hands, that is, unwashed—
verses.7:3: for the Pharisees and all the Jews do not eat unless they wash their hands with the fist, holding fast to the tradition of the elders,
verses.7:4: and when coming from the marketplace, they do not eat unless they wash themselves; and there are many other things that they received to hold fast to, washings of cups and pitchers and copper vessels—
verses.7:5: and the Pharisees and the scribes asked Him, "Why do Your disciples not walk according to the tradition of the elders, but eat bread with defiled hands?"
verses.7:6: And He said to them, "Isaiah prophesied rightly about you hypocrites, as it is written, 'This people honors Me with their lips, but their heart is far away from Me;
verses.7:7: and in vain they worship Me, teaching as doctrines the precepts of men.'
verses.7:8: Abandoning the commandment of God, you hold fast to the tradition of men."
verses.7:9: And He was saying to them, "How well you set aside the commandment of God so that you may keep your tradition!
verses.7:10: For Moses said, 'Honor your father and your mother,' and, 'The one who speaks evil of father or mother must surely die.'
verses.7:11: But you say that if a man says to his father or his mother, 'Whatever you might profit from me is Corban'—that is, a gift—
verses.7:12: you no longer permit him to do anything for his father or his mother,
verses.7:13: nullifying the word of God by your tradition that you have handed down; and you do many similar things like this."
verses.7:14: And calling the crowd to Himself again, He was saying to them, "Listen to Me, all of you, and understand.
verses.7:15: There is nothing outside a person that, going into him, can defile him; rather, the things coming out of a person are the things that defile the person."
verses.7:17: And when He entered a house away from the crowd, His disciples were asking Him about the parable.
verses.7:18: And He said to them, "Are you also so lacking in understanding? Do you not perceive that whatever goes into a person from outside cannot defile him,
verses.7:19: because it does not go into his heart, but into his stomach, and goes out into the latrine?"—declaring all foods clean.
verses.7:20: And He was saying, "What comes out of a person, that is what defiles the person.
verses.7:21: For from within, out of the heart of people, evil thoughts come out: sexual immoralities, thefts, murders, adulteries,
verses.7:22: acts of greed, acts of wickedness, deceit, licentiousness, an evil eye, slander, arrogance, foolishness.
verses.7:23: All these evil things come out from within and defile the person."
verses.7:24: And getting up from there, He went away into the region of Tyre and Sidon. And entering a house, He wanted no one to know, yet He could not escape notice.
verses.7:25: Instead, immediately a woman whose little daughter had an unclean spirit heard about Him, and she came and fell down at His feet.
verses.7:26: Now the woman was Greek, a Syrophoenician by birth; and she kept asking Him to cast the demon out of her daughter.
verses.7:27: And He was saying to her, "Let the children be filled first, for it is not good to take the bread of the children and throw it to the little dogs."
verses.7:28: But she answered and said to Him, "Yes, Lord; even the little dogs under the table eat from the crumbs of the children."
verses.7:29: And He said to her, "Because of this word, go; the demon has gone out of your daughter."
verses.7:30: And going away to her house, she found the child lying on the bed, and the demon gone out.
verses.7:31: And going out again from the region of Tyre, He came through Sidon to the Sea of Galilee, through the middle of the region of Decapolis.
verses.7:32: And they brought to Him a man who was deaf and spoke with difficulty, and they implored Him to lay His hand on him.
verses.7:33: And taking him aside from the crowd privately, He put His fingers into his ears, and after spitting, He touched his tongue;
verses.7:34: and looking up to heaven, He sighed and said to him, "Ephphatha," that is, "Be opened!"
verses.7:35: And his ears were opened, and the bond of his tongue was loosed, and he began speaking plainly.
verses.7:36: And He ordered them to tell no one; yet the more He ordered them, all the more abundantly they kept proclaiming it.
verses.7:37: And they were astonished beyond all measure, saying, "He has done all things well; He makes both the deaf hear and the mute speak."
verses.8:1: In those days, when there was again a large crowd and they had nothing to eat, calling His disciples to Himself, He said to them,
verses.8:2: "I feel compassion for the crowd, because they have remained with Me for three days already and have nothing to eat.
verses.8:3: And if I send them away hungry to their homes, they will faint on the way; and some of them have come from far away."
verses.8:4: And His disciples answered Him, "Where will anyone be able to satisfy these people with bread here in a desolate place?"
verses.8:5: And He asked them, "How many loaves do you have?" And they said, "Seven."
verses.8:6: And He instructed the crowd to recline on the ground; and taking the seven loaves, after giving thanks, He broke them and kept giving them to His disciples to serve, and they served them to the crowd.
verses.8:7: They also had a few small fish; and after blessing them, He told them to serve these as well.
verses.8:8: And they ate and were satisfied; and they picked up seven large baskets of leftover broken pieces.
verses.8:9: Now there were about four thousand people. And He sent them away.
verses.8:10: And immediately getting into the boat with His disciples, He came to the region of Dalmanutha.
verses.8:11: And the Pharisees came out and began to debate with Him, seeking from Him a sign from heaven, testing Him.
verses.8:12: And sighing deeply in His spirit, He said, "Why does this generation seek a sign? Truly I say to you, no sign will be given to this generation."
verses.8:13: And leaving them, embarking again, He departed to the other side.
verses.8:14: And they had forgotten to bring bread, and except for one loaf, they had none with them in the boat.
verses.8:15: And He was cautioning them, saying, "Watch out! Beware of the leaven of the Pharisees and the leaven of Herod."
verses.8:16: And they were reasoning with one another because they had no bread.
verses.8:17: And aware of this, Jesus said to them, "Why are you reasoning because you have no bread? Do you not yet perceive or understand? Do you have your heart hardened?
verses.8:18: Having eyes, do you not see, and having ears, do you not hear? And do you not remember,
verses.8:19: when I broke the five loaves for the five thousand, how many baskets full of broken pieces you picked up?" They said to Him, "Twelve."
verses.8:20: "And when I broke the seven for the four thousand, how many large basketfuls of broken pieces did you pick up?" And they said, "Seven."
verses.8:21: And He said to them, "How do you not yet understand?"
verses.8:22: And they came to Bethsaida. And they brought a blind man to Him and begged Him to touch him.
verses.8:23: And taking hold of the blind man's hand, He led him outside the village; and after spitting on his eyes and laying His hands on him, He asked him, "Do you see anything?"
verses.8:24: And looking up, he said, "I see people, for I see them like trees, walking around."
verses.8:25: Then again He laid His hands on his eyes; and he looked intently and was restored, and began to see everything clearly.
verses.8:26: And He sent him to his home, saying, "Do not even enter the village."
verses.8:27: And Jesus and His disciples went out to the villages of Caesarea Philippi; and on the way He asked His disciples, saying to them, "Who do people say that I am?"
verses.8:28: And they told Him, saying, "John the Baptist; and others say Elijah; and others, one of the prophets."
verses.8:29: And He asked them, "But who do you say that I am?" Peter answered and said to Him, "You are the Christ."
verses.8:30: And He sternly warned them to tell no one about Him.
verses.8:31: And He began to teach them that the Son of Man must suffer many things and be rejected by the elders and the chief priests and the scribes, and be killed, and after three days rise.
verses.8:32: And He was speaking the word plainly. And taking Him aside, Peter began to rebuke Him.
verses.8:33: But turning around and seeing His disciples, He rebuked Peter and said, "Get behind Me, Satan! For you are not setting your mind on the things of God, but on the things of human beings."
verses.8:34: And calling the crowd to Himself along with His disciples, He said to them, "If anyone wants to come after Me, he must deny himself, take up his cross, and follow Me.
verses.8:35: For whoever wants to save his life will lose it, but whoever loses his life on account of Me and the gospel will save it.
verses.8:36: For what does it benefit a person to gain the entire world and forfeit his life?
verses.8:37: For what could a person give in exchange for his life?
verses.8:38: For whoever is ashamed of Me and My words in this adulterous and sinful generation, the Son of Man will also be ashamed of him when He comes in the glory of His Father with the holy angels."
verses.9:1: And He was saying to them, "Truly I say to you that there are some of those standing here who will by no means taste death until they see the kingdom of God having come in power."
verses.9:2: And after six days, Jesus took Peter and James and John with Him and led them up onto a high mountain privately by themselves; and He was transfigured before them,
verses.9:3: and His garments became gleaming, intensely white, so white that no launderer on the earth is able to whiten them like that.
verses.9:4: And Elijah appeared to them with Moses, and they were conversing with Jesus.
verses.9:5: And Peter responded and said to Jesus, "Rabbi, it is good for us to be here; and let us make three tents, one for You, and one for Moses, and one for Elijah."
verses.9:6: For he did not know what to answer, because they had become terrified.
verses.9:7: And a cloud formed, overshadowing them, and a voice came out of the cloud: "This is My beloved Son; listen to Him."
verses.9:8: And suddenly, looking around, they no longer saw anyone except Jesus alone with them.
verses.9:9: And as they were coming down from the mountain, He instructed them to tell no one the things they had seen, except after the Son of Man has risen from the dead.
verses.9:10: And they kept this saying to themselves, discussing what rising from the dead meant.
verses.9:11: And they were questioning Him, saying, "Why do the scribes say that Elijah must come first?"
verses.9:12: And He said to them, "Elijah indeed comes first and restores all things; and how is it written concerning the Son of Man that He should suffer many things and be treated with contempt?
verses.9:13: But I tell you that Elijah has indeed come, and they did to him whatever they wished, just as it is written concerning him."
verses.9:14: And when they came to the disciples, they saw a large crowd around them and scribes debating with them.
verses.9:15: And immediately the entire crowd, upon seeing Him, were greatly amazed, and running up, they were greeting Him.
verses.9:16: And He questioned them, "What are you debating among yourselves?"
verses.9:17: And one from the crowd answered Him, "Teacher, I brought my son to You, who has a mute spirit;
verses.9:18: and wherever it seizes him, it slams him down, and he foams at the mouth and grinds his teeth and becomes rigid; and I spoke to Your disciples to cast it out, and they were not able."
verses.9:19: And answering them, He said, "O unbelieving generation, how long will I be with you? How long will I put up with you? Bring him to Me."
verses.9:20: And they brought him to Him. And when the spirit saw Him, immediately it convulsed him violently, and falling upon the ground, he was rolling about, foaming at the mouth.
verses.9:21: And He questioned his father, "How long a time has it been since this happened to him?" And he said, "From childhood;
verses.9:22: and often it threw him both into fire and into waters in order to destroy him. But if You can do anything, have compassion on us and help us."
verses.9:23: And Jesus said to him, "'If You can'! All things are possible for the one who believes."
verses.9:24: Immediately the father of the child cried out and was saying, "I believe; help my unbelief!"
verses.9:25: And when Jesus saw that a crowd was running together, He rebuked the unclean spirit, saying to it, "You mute and deaf spirit, I command you, come out of him and never enter into him again."
verses.9:26: And crying out and convulsing him greatly, it came out; and he became like one dead, so that most of them were saying that he had died.
verses.9:27: But Jesus, taking hold of his hand, raised him up, and he stood up.
verses.9:28: And when He had entered a house, His disciples were questioning Him privately, "Why were we not able to cast it out?"
verses.9:29: And He said to them, "This kind cannot come out by anything except by prayer."
verses.9:30: And going out from there, they were passing through Galilee, and He did not want anyone to know;
verses.9:31: for He was teaching His disciples and saying to them, "The Son of Man is being handed over into the hands of men, and they will kill Him; and when He has been killed, after three days He will rise."
verses.9:32: But they did not understand the statement, and they were afraid to question Him.
verses.9:33: And they came to Capernaum. And when He was in the house, He questioned them, "What were you discussing on the way?"
verses.9:34: But they kept silent, for on the way they had argued with one another about who was the greatest.
verses.9:35: And sitting down, He called the twelve and said to them, "If anyone wishes to be first, he shall be last of all and servant of all."
verses.9:36: And taking a child, He set him in their midst; and taking him in His arms, He said to them,
verses.9:37: "Whoever receives one of such children in My name receives Me; and whoever receives Me does not receive Me, but the One who sent Me."
verses.9:38: John said to Him, "Teacher, we saw someone casting out demons in Your name, and we were trying to stop him, because he was not following us."
verses.9:39: But Jesus said, "Do not stop him, for there is no one who will perform a mighty work in My name and be able soon afterward to speak evil of Me.
verses.9:40: For anyone who is not against us is for us.
verses.9:41: For whoever gives you a cup of water to drink on account of the name, because you belong to Christ, truly I say to you that he will by no means lose his reward.
verses.9:42: And whoever causes one of these little ones who believe in Me to stumble, it would be better for him if a donkey-turned millstone were hung around his neck and he were thrown into the sea.
verses.9:43: And if your hand causes you to stumble, cut it off; it is better for you to enter into life maimed than, having two hands, to go away into Gehenna, into the unquenchable fire.
verses.9:45: And if your foot causes you to stumble, cut it off; it is better for you to enter into life lame than, having two feet, to be thrown into Gehenna.
verses.9:47: And if your eye causes you to stumble, throw it out; it is better for you to enter into the kingdom of God with one eye than, having two eyes, to be thrown into Gehenna,
verses.9:48: where their worm does not perish, and the fire is not quenched.
verses.9:49: For everyone will be salted with fire.
verses.9:50: Salt is good; but if the salt becomes unsalty, with what will you season it? Have salt in yourselves, and be at peace with one another."
verses.10:1: And rising from there, He went into the region of Judea and beyond the Jordan, and crowds gathered to Him again, and as He was accustomed, He was teaching them again.
verses.10:2: And Pharisees approached and were questioning Him whether it is lawful for a husband to divorce a wife, testing Him.
verses.10:3: And answering, He said to them, "What did Moses command you?"
verses.10:4: And they said, "Moses permitted writing a certificate of divorce and divorcing her."
verses.10:5: And Jesus said to them, "Because of your hardness of heart he wrote this commandment for you.
verses.10:6: But from the beginning of creation, He made them male and female.
verses.10:7: For this reason a man will leave his father and his mother,
verses.10:8: and the two will become one flesh; so that they are no longer two, but one flesh.
verses.10:9: Therefore, what God joined together, let no human separate."
verses.10:10: And in the house, the disciples were questioning Him again about this.
verses.10:11: And He said to them, "Whoever divorces his wife and marries another woman commits adultery against her;
verses.10:12: and if she divorces her husband and marries another man, she commits adultery."
verses.10:13: And they were bringing young children to Him so that He might touch them, but the disciples rebuked them.
verses.10:14: But when Jesus saw this, He was indignant and said to them, "Allow the young children to come to Me; do not hinder them, for to such as these belongs the kingdom of God.
verses.10:15: Truly I say to you, whoever does not receive the kingdom of God like a young child will by no means enter it."
verses.10:16: And taking them into His arms, He kept blessing them, laying His hands on them.
verses.10:17: And as He was setting out onto the road, someone ran up, knelt before Him, and asked Him, "Good Teacher, what should I do so that I may inherit eternal life?"
verses.10:18: And Jesus said to him, "Why do you call Me good? No one is good except One, God.
verses.10:19: You know the commandments: 'Do not murder, do not commit adultery, do not steal, do not bear false witness, do not defraud, honor your father and mother.'"
verses.10:20: And he said to Him, "Teacher, all these things I have kept from my youth."
verses.10:21: And Jesus, looking intently at him, loved him and said to him, "One thing you lack: go, sell whatever you have and give to the poor, and you will have treasure in heaven; and come, follow Me."
verses.10:22: Becoming downcast at this statement, he went away grieving, for he was one who owned many possessions.
verses.10:23: And looking around, Jesus said to His disciples, "How difficult it will be for those who have wealth to enter the kingdom of God!"
verses.10:24: And the disciples were amazed at His words. But Jesus answered again and said to them, "Children, how difficult it is to enter the kingdom of God!
verses.10:25: It is easier for a camel to pass through the eye of a needle than for a rich person to enter the kingdom of God."
verses.10:26: And they were extraordinarily astonished, saying to Him, "Then who can be saved?"
verses.10:27: Looking intently at them, Jesus said, "With people it is impossible, but not with God; for all things are possible with God."
verses.10:28: Peter began to say to Him, "Look, we have left everything and followed You."
verses.10:29: Jesus said, "Truly I say to you, there is no one who has left house or brothers or sisters or mother or father or children or fields on account of Me and the gospel,
verses.10:30: who will not receive a hundred times as much now in this present time, houses and brothers and sisters and mothers and children and fields, along with persecutions, and in the age to come, eternal life.
verses.10:31: But many who are first will be last, and the last will be first."
verses.10:32: Now they were on the road going up to Jerusalem, and Jesus was walking ahead of them; and they were amazed, while those who followed were afraid. And taking the twelve aside again, He began to tell them the things that were about to happen to Him,
verses.10:33: "Look, we are going up to Jerusalem, and the Son of Man will be handed over to the chief priests and the scribes, and they will condemn Him to death and hand Him over to the Gentiles;
verses.10:34: and they will mock Him and spit on Him and flog Him and kill Him, and after three days He will rise."
verses.10:35: And James and John, the sons of Zebedee, came up to Him, saying to Him, "Teacher, we want You to do for us whatever we ask of You."
verses.10:36: And He said to them, "What do you want Me to do for you?"
verses.10:37: And they said to Him, "Grant us that we may sit, one at Your right and one at Your left, in Your glory."
verses.10:38: But Jesus said to them, "You do not know what you are asking. Are you able to drink the cup that I drink, or to be baptized with the baptism with which I am baptized?"
verses.10:39: And they said to Him, "We are able." And Jesus said to them, "The cup that I drink you will drink, and with the baptism with which I am baptized you will be baptized;
verses.10:40: but to sit at My right or at My left is not Mine to grant, but it is for those for whom it has been prepared."
verses.10:41: And when the ten heard this, they began to be indignant about James and John.
verses.10:42: And calling them to Himself, Jesus said to them, "You know that those who are recognized as rulers of the Gentiles lord it over them, and their great ones exercise authority over them.
verses.10:43: But it is not this way among you; rather, whoever wants to become great among you will be your servant,
verses.10:44: and whoever wants to be first among you will be slave of all.
verses.10:45: For even the Son of Man did not come to be served, but to serve, and to give His life as a ransom in place of many."
verses.10:46: And they came to Jericho. And as He was leaving Jericho with His disciples and a sizable crowd, the son of Timaeus, Bartimaeus, a blind beggar, was sitting beside the road.
verses.10:47: And when he heard that it was Jesus the Nazarene, he began to cry out and say, "Son of David, Jesus, have mercy on me!"
verses.10:48: And many were rebuking him to make him be silent, but he kept crying out all the more, "Son of David, have mercy on me!"
verses.10:49: And Jesus stopped and said, "Call him." And they called the blind man, saying to him, "Take courage, get up; He is calling you."
verses.10:50: And throwing off his cloak, he sprang up and came to Jesus.
verses.10:51: And answering him, Jesus said, "What do you want Me to do for you?" And the blind man said to Him, "Rabboni, that I may regain my sight."
verses.10:52: And Jesus said to him, "Go, your faith has saved you." And immediately he regained his sight and was following Him on the road.
verses.11:1: And when they were approaching Jerusalem, at Bethphage and Bethany near the Mount of Olives, He sent two of His disciples
verses.11:2: and said to them, "Go into the village opposite you, and immediately as you enter it, you will find a colt tied on which no person has yet sat; untie it and bring it.
verses.11:3: And if anyone says to you, 'Why are you doing this?' say, 'The Lord has need of it, and immediately He will send it back here.'"
verses.11:4: And they went away and found a colt tied by the door outside on the street, and they untied it.
verses.11:5: And some of those standing there were saying to them, "What are you doing, untying the colt?"
verses.11:6: And they spoke to them just as Jesus had said, and they let them go.
verses.11:7: And they brought the colt to Jesus and placed their cloaks on it, and He sat on it.
verses.11:8: And many spread their cloaks on the road, and others leafy branches that they had cut from the fields.
verses.11:9: And those going ahead and those following were crying out, "Hosanna! Blessed is the One who comes in the name of the Lord!
verses.11:10: Blessed is the coming kingdom of our father David! Hosanna in the highest!"
verses.11:11: And He entered Jerusalem, into the temple; and after looking around at everything, since the hour was already late, He went out to Bethany with the twelve.
verses.11:12: And on the next day, when they had come out from Bethany, He became hungry.
verses.11:13: And seeing from a distance a fig tree that had leaves, He went to see if perhaps He would find anything on it; and when He came to it, He found nothing except leaves, for it was not the season for figs.
verses.11:14: And answering, He said to it, "May no one ever eat fruit from you again!" And His disciples were listening.
verses.11:15: And they came to Jerusalem. And entering the temple, He began to drive out those who were selling and those who were buying in the temple, and He overturned the tables of the moneychangers and the seats of those who were selling the doves,
verses.11:16: and He would not allow anyone to carry any object through the temple.
verses.11:17: And He was teaching and saying to them, "Is it not written, 'My house will be called a house of prayer for all the nations'? But you have made it a cave of robbers."
verses.11:18: And the chief priests and the scribes heard it, and they were seeking how they might destroy Him; for they feared Him, because the entire crowd was astonished at His teaching.
verses.11:19: And whenever evening came, they would go outside the city.
verses.11:20: And as they were passing by in the morning, they saw the fig tree withered from the roots.
verses.11:21: And remembering, Peter said to Him, "Rabbi, look! The fig tree that You cursed has withered!"
verses.11:22: And answering, Jesus said to them, "Have faith in God.
verses.11:23: Truly I say to you that whoever says to this mountain, 'Be lifted up and thrown into the sea,' and does not doubt in his heart, but believes that what he speaks will come about, it will be done for him.
verses.11:24: For this reason I say to you, all things that you pray and ask for, believe that you have received them, and they will be yours.
verses.11:25: And whenever you stand praying, forgive if you have anything against anyone, so that your Father who is in heaven may also forgive you your transgressions."
verses.11:27: And they came again to Jerusalem. And as He was walking in the temple, the chief priests and the scribes and the elders came to Him,
verses.11:28: and they were saying to Him, "By what authority are You doing these things? Or who gave You this authority to do these things?"
verses.11:29: And Jesus said to them, "I will also ask you one question; answer Me, and I will tell you by what authority I do these things:
verses.11:30: The baptism of John—was it from heaven or from people? Answer Me."
verses.11:31: And they were reasoning among themselves, saying, "If we say, 'From heaven,' He will say, 'Why then did you not believe him?'
verses.11:32: But should we say, 'From people'?"—they were afraid of the crowd, for everyone held that John truly was a prophet.
verses.11:33: And answering Jesus, they said, "We do not know." And Jesus said to them, "Neither am I telling you by what authority I do these things."
verses.12:1: And He began to speak to them in parables: "A man planted a vineyard, and set a fence around it, and dug a pit for a winepress, and built a tower, and leased it out to farmers, and went away on a journey.
verses.12:2: And at the proper time he sent a slave to the farmers, so that he might receive from the farmers some of the fruit of the vineyard.
verses.12:3: And taking him, they beat him and sent him away empty-handed.
verses.12:4: And again he sent another slave to them; and that one they struck on the head and treated shamefully.
verses.12:5: And he sent another, and that one they killed; and many others as well, beating some and killing others.
verses.12:6: He still had one more, a beloved son; he sent him last to them, saying, 'They will respect my son.'
verses.12:7: But those farmers said among themselves, 'This is the heir; come, let us kill him, and the inheritance will be ours.'
verses.12:8: And taking him, they killed him and threw him out of the vineyard.
verses.12:9: What then will the owner of the vineyard do? He will come and destroy the farmers, and will give the vineyard to others.
verses.12:10: Have you not even read this Scripture: 'The stone that the builders rejected, this one has become the head of the corner;
verses.12:11: this came about from the Lord, and it is marvelous in our eyes'?"
verses.12:12: And they were seeking to seize Him, yet they feared the crowd, for they knew that He had spoken the parable against them. And leaving Him, they went away.
verses.12:13: And they sent to Him some of the Pharisees and of the Herodians, in order that they might trap Him in speech.
verses.12:14: And coming, they said to Him, "Teacher, we know that You are truthful and do not defer to anyone, for You do not look at the face of people, but in truth You teach the way of God. Is it lawful to pay a poll tax to Caesar, or not? Should we pay, or should we not pay?"
verses.12:15: But knowing their hypocrisy, He said to them, "Why are you testing Me? Bring Me a denarius so that I may see it."
verses.12:16: And they brought one. And He said to them, "Whose image and inscription is this?" And they said to Him, "Caesar's."
verses.12:17: And Jesus said to them, "Pay back to Caesar the things that belong to Caesar, and to God the things that belong to God." And they were utterly amazed at Him.
verses.12:18: And Sadducees came to Him, who say that there is no resurrection, and they questioned Him, saying,
verses.12:19: "Teacher, Moses wrote for us that if a man's brother dies and leaves behind a wife and leaves no child, his brother is to take the wife and raise up offspring for his brother.
verses.12:20: There were seven brothers; and the first took a wife, and when dying left no offspring.
verses.12:21: And the second took her, and died without leaving behind offspring, and the third likewise;
verses.12:22: and the seven left no offspring. Last of all, the woman also died.
verses.12:23: In the resurrection, when they rise, whose wife among them will she be? For the seven had her as a wife."
verses.12:24: Jesus said to them, "Is this not the reason you are in error, because you know neither the Scriptures nor the power of God?
verses.12:25: For when they rise from the dead, they neither marry nor are given in marriage, but are like angels in the heavens.
verses.12:26: But concerning the dead, that they are raised, have you not read in the book of Moses, at the bush, how God spoke to him, saying, 'I am the God of Abraham, and the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob'?
verses.12:27: He is not the God of the dead, but of the living; you are greatly in error."
verses.12:28: And one of the scribes approached, having heard them disputing, and seeing that He had answered them well, he asked Him, "Which commandment is first of all?"
verses.12:29: Jesus answered, "The first is: 'Listen, Israel: the Lord our God, the Lord is one,
verses.12:30: and you shall love the Lord your God with your whole heart, and with your whole soul, and with your whole mind, and with your whole strength.'
verses.12:31: The second is this: 'You shall love your neighbor as yourself.' There is no other commandment greater than these."
verses.12:32: And the scribe said to Him, "Well said, Teacher; in truth You have spoken, that He is one, and there is no other besides Him;
verses.12:33: and to love Him with the whole heart, and with the whole understanding, and with the whole strength, and to love one's neighbor as oneself, is more than all whole burnt offerings and sacrifices."
verses.12:34: And Jesus, seeing that he had answered sensibly, said to him, "You are not far from the kingdom of God." And no one dared any longer to question Him.
verses.12:35: And responding, Jesus was saying as He taught in the temple, "How is it that the scribes say that the Christ is the son of David?
verses.12:36: David himself said in the Holy Spirit, 'The Lord said to my Lord, "Sit at My right hand, until I place Your enemies beneath Your feet."'
verses.12:37: David himself calls Him Lord, and how is He his son?" And the large crowd was listening to Him gladly.
verses.12:38: And in His teaching He was saying, "Watch out for the scribes, who like to walk around in long robes, and who desire greetings in the marketplaces,
verses.12:39: and front seats in the synagogues, and places of honor at banquets,
verses.12:40: who devour the houses of widows, and for a pretense pray at length; these will receive a more severe judgment."
verses.12:41: And sitting down opposite the treasury, He was observing how the crowd was putting money into the treasury; and many rich people were putting in large amounts.
verses.12:42: And one poor widow came and put in two lepta, which is a quadrans.
verses.12:43: And calling His disciples to Himself, He said to them, "Truly I say to you, this poor widow has put in more than all those who are putting into the treasury;
verses.12:44: for they all put in out of their surplus, but she out of her poverty put in everything that she had, her whole livelihood."
verses.13:1: And as He was going out of the temple, one of His disciples said to Him, "Teacher, look! What remarkable stones and what remarkable buildings!"
verses.13:2: And Jesus said to him, "Do you see these great buildings? Not a stone will be left here upon a stone that will not be torn down."
verses.13:3: And as He was sitting on the Mount of Olives opposite the temple, Peter, James, John, and Andrew began questioning Him privately:
verses.13:4: "Tell us when these things will happen, and what the sign will be when all these things are about to be brought to completion."
verses.13:5: And Jesus began to say to them, "Watch out that no one misleads you.
verses.13:6: Many will come in My name, saying, 'I am,' and they will mislead many.
verses.13:7: Now when you hear of wars and reports of wars, do not be alarmed; this must take place, but the end is not yet.
verses.13:8: For nation will rise against nation, and kingdom against kingdom; there will be earthquakes in various places; there will be famines. These are the beginning of birth pains.
verses.13:9: But you, watch out for yourselves; they will hand you over to councils, and in synagogues you will be beaten, and you will stand before governors and kings on account of Me, as a testimony to them.
verses.13:10: And the gospel must first be proclaimed to all the nations.
verses.13:11: And when they lead you away and hand you over, do not be anxious beforehand about what you should speak, but whatever is given to you in that hour, speak that; for it is not you who are speaking, but the Holy Spirit.
verses.13:12: And brother will hand over brother to death, and a father his child, and children will rise up against parents and put them to death.
verses.13:13: And you will be hated by all because of My name. But the one who endures to the end, that one will be saved.
verses.13:14: Now when you see the abomination of desolation standing where it ought not to be (let the reader understand), then let those who are in Judea flee to the mountains;
verses.13:15: and let the one who is on the housetop not go down, nor enter to take anything out of his house;
verses.13:16: and let the one who is in the field not turn back to take his cloak.
verses.13:17: And woe to those who are pregnant and to those who are nursing in those days.
verses.13:18: But pray that it may not happen in winter.
verses.13:19: For those days will be an affliction such as has not occurred from the beginning of the creation that God created until now, and will by no means ever occur.
verses.13:20: And if the Lord had not cut short the days, no flesh would have been saved. But for the sake of the chosen ones whom He chose, He cut short the days.
verses.13:21: And then if anyone says to you, 'Look, here is the Christ!' 'Look, there!' do not believe it.
verses.13:22: For false christs and false prophets will arise and will produce signs and wonders in order to lead astray, if possible, the chosen ones.
verses.13:23: But you, watch out; see, I have told you everything beforehand.
verses.13:24: But in those days, after that affliction, the sun will be darkened, and the moon will not give its radiance,
verses.13:25: and the stars will be falling from heaven, and the powers that are in the heavens will be shaken.
verses.13:26: And then they will see the Son of Man coming in clouds with great power and glory.
verses.13:27: And then He will send out the angels and will gather together His chosen ones from the four winds, from the end of earth to the end of heaven.
verses.13:28: Now learn the parable from the fig tree: when its branch has already become tender and puts forth its leaves, you know that summer is near.
verses.13:29: So you also, when you see these things taking place, know that it is near, at the doors.
verses.13:30: Truly I say to you, this generation will by no means pass away until all these things take place.
verses.13:31: Heaven and earth will pass away, but My words will by no means pass away.
verses.13:32: But concerning that day or the hour, no one knows, not even the angels in heaven, nor the Son, except the Father.
verses.13:33: Watch out, stay alert, and pray, for you do not know when the time is.
verses.13:34: It is like a man away on a journey, who left his house and gave his slaves the authority, to each his work, and commanded the doorkeeper to stay awake.
verses.13:35: Therefore stay awake, for you do not know when the master of the house is coming, whether in the evening, or at midnight, or at the crowing of the rooster, or in the morning,
verses.13:36: so that he may not come suddenly and find you sleeping.
verses.13:37: And what I say to you, I say to all: stay awake!"
verses.14:1: Now it was two days until the Passover and the Unleavened Bread. And the chief priests and the scribes were seeking how they might seize Him by deceit and kill Him.
verses.14:2: For they were saying, "Not during the feast, or else there will be an uproar of the people."
verses.14:3: And while He was in Bethany, in the house of Simon the leper, as He was reclining at table, a woman came with an alabaster jar of very costly perfume of genuine nard. After breaking the alabaster jar, she poured it over His head.
verses.14:4: But some were indignant among themselves: "Why has this waste of the perfume taken place?
verses.14:5: For this perfume could have been sold for more than three hundred denarii and given to the poor." And they were scolding her.
verses.14:6: But Jesus said, "Leave her alone. Why are you causing her trouble? She has performed a good work for Me.
verses.14:7: For you always have the poor with you, and whenever you wish you are able to do good to them, but you do not always have Me.
verses.14:8: What she was able to do, she did; she anointed My body in advance for burial.
verses.14:9: And truly I say to you, wherever the gospel is proclaimed throughout the whole world, what this woman did will also be spoken of as a memorial of her."
verses.14:10: And Judas Iscariot, one of the twelve, went off to the chief priests so that he might hand Him over to them.
verses.14:11: And when they heard this, they rejoiced and promised to give him money. And he was seeking how he might hand Him over at an opportune time.
verses.14:12: And on the first day of Unleavened Bread, when they would sacrifice the Passover, His disciples said to Him, "Where do You wish us to go and prepare so that You may eat the Passover?"
verses.14:13: And He sent two of His disciples and said to them, "Go into the city, and a man carrying a pitcher of water will meet you. Follow him,
verses.14:14: and wherever he enters, tell the owner of the house that the Teacher says, 'Where is My guest room where I may eat the Passover with My disciples?'
verses.14:15: And he himself will show you a large upper room, furnished and ready; and prepare for us there."
verses.14:16: And the disciples went out and came into the city, and they found things just as He had told them, and they prepared the Passover.
verses.14:17: And when evening came, He arrived with the twelve.
verses.14:18: And while they were reclining and eating, Jesus said, "Truly I say to you that one of you will hand Me over, one who is eating with Me."
verses.14:19: They began to be grieved and to say to Him one by one, "Surely not I?"
verses.14:20: And He said to them, "It is one of the twelve, the one dipping with Me into the bowl.
verses.14:21: For the Son of Man goes just as it has been written concerning Him, yet woe to that man through whom the Son of Man is handed over! It would have been good for him if that man had not been born."
verses.14:22: And while they were eating, He took bread, and after blessing, He broke it and gave it to them, and said, "Take; this is My body."
verses.14:23: And taking a cup, after giving thanks, He gave it to them, and they all drank from it.
verses.14:24: And He said to them, "This is My blood of the covenant, which is poured out on behalf of many.
verses.14:25: Truly I say to you that I will by no means drink again of the fruit of the vine until that day when I drink it new in the kingdom of God."
verses.14:26: And having sung a hymn, they went out to the Mount of Olives.
verses.14:27: And Jesus said to them, "You will all stumble, because it has been written, 'I will strike the shepherd, and the sheep will be scattered.'
verses.14:28: Yet after I have been raised, I will go ahead of you into Galilee."
verses.14:29: But Peter said to Him, "Even if all will stumble, yet not I."
verses.14:30: And Jesus said to him, "Truly I say to you that today, this night, before a rooster crows twice, you yourself will deny Me three times."
verses.14:31: But he kept speaking emphatically, "If I must die with You, I will by no means deny You." And all of them were saying the same thing as well.
verses.14:32: And they came to a place whose name was Gethsemane, and He said to His disciples, "Sit here while I pray."
verses.14:33: And He took Peter and James and John along with Him, and began to be deeply dismayed and in anguish.
verses.14:34: And He said to them, "My soul is exceedingly sorrowful, to the point of death; stay here and keep awake."
verses.14:35: And going a little farther, He fell on the ground and was praying that, if it were possible, the hour might pass away from Him.
verses.14:36: And He was saying, "Abba, Father, all things are possible for You; take this cup away from Me; yet not what I wish, but what You wish."
verses.14:37: And He came and found them sleeping, and said to Peter, "Simon, are you sleeping? Were you not able to keep awake for one hour?
verses.14:38: Keep awake and pray, so that you may not come into temptation; the spirit indeed is eager, yet the flesh is weak."
verses.14:39: And going away again, He prayed, speaking the same words.
verses.14:40: And coming again, He found them sleeping, for their eyes were weighed down, and they did not know what to answer Him.
verses.14:41: And He came the third time and said to them, "Are you still sleeping and taking your rest? It is enough! The hour has come; look, the Son of Man is being handed over into the hands of sinners.
verses.14:42: Get up, let us go; look, the one handing Me over has drawn near."
verses.14:43: And immediately, while He was still speaking, Judas, one of the twelve, arrived, and with him a crowd with swords and clubs, from the chief priests and the scribes and the elders.
verses.14:44: Now the one handing Him over had given them an agreed signal, saying, "The one whom I kiss, He is the one; seize Him and lead Him away securely."
verses.14:45: And when he arrived, he immediately stepped up to Him and said, "Rabbi," and kissed Him.
verses.14:46: And they laid their hands on Him and seized Him.
verses.14:47: But a certain one of those standing by drew his sword, struck the slave of the high priest, and cut off his ear.
verses.14:48: And answering, Jesus said to them, "Have you come out as against a robber with swords and clubs to arrest Me?
verses.14:49: Day by day I was with you in the temple teaching, and you did not seize Me; yet this is so that the Scriptures may be fulfilled."
verses.14:50: And leaving Him, they all fled.
verses.14:51: And a certain young man was following along with Him, wearing a linen cloth over his naked body, and they seized him.
verses.14:52: But leaving the linen cloth behind, he fled naked.
verses.14:53: And they led Jesus away to the high priest, and all the chief priests and the elders and the scribes gathered together.
verses.14:54: And Peter followed Him from a distance, right inside into the courtyard of the high priest, and he was sitting with the officers and warming himself by the firelight.
verses.14:55: Now the chief priests and the whole Sanhedrin were seeking testimony against Jesus in order to put Him to death, and they were not finding any.
verses.14:56: For many were giving false testimony against Him, and the testimonies were not consistent.
verses.14:57: And some stood up and were giving false testimony against Him, saying,
verses.14:58: "We heard Him say, 'I will destroy this temple made with hands, and in three days I will build another not made with hands.'"
verses.14:59: And not even on this point was their testimony consistent.
verses.14:60: And standing up in the center, the high priest questioned Jesus, saying, "Do You answer nothing? What is it that these men are testifying against You?"
verses.14:61: But He kept silent and answered nothing. Again the high priest was questioning Him and said to Him, "Are You the Christ, the Son of the Blessed One?"
verses.14:62: And Jesus said, "I am; and you will see the Son of Man sitting at the right hand of the Power and coming with the clouds of heaven."
verses.14:63: Then the high priest, tearing his garments, said, "What further need do we have of witnesses?
verses.14:64: You have heard the blasphemy. How does it seem to you?" And they all condemned Him to be deserving of death.
verses.14:65: And some began to spit on Him and to cover His face and to strike Him with their fists and to say to Him, "Prophesy!" And the officers received Him with slaps.
verses.14:66: And while Peter was below in the courtyard, one of the servant girls of the high priest came,
verses.14:67: and seeing Peter warming himself, she looked intently at him and said, "You also were with the Nazarene, Jesus."
verses.14:68: But he denied it, saying, "I neither know nor understand what you are saying." And he went outside into the forecourt.
verses.14:69: And when the servant girl saw him, she began again to say to those standing by, "This man is one of them."
verses.14:70: But he was denying it again. And after a little while, those standing by were again saying to Peter, "Truly you are one of them, for you are a Galilean as well."
verses.14:71: But he began to invoke curses and to swear, "I do not know this man whom you are speaking of."
verses.14:72: And immediately a rooster crowed a second time. And Peter remembered the word, how Jesus had said to him, "Before a rooster crows twice, you will deny Me three times." And breaking down, he wept.
verses.15:1: And immediately, early in the morning, the chief priests with the elders and scribes and the entire Sanhedrin held a consultation; and having bound Jesus, they led Him away and handed Him over to Pilate.
verses.15:2: And Pilate questioned Him, "Are You the King of the Jews?" And answering him, He said, "You say so."
verses.15:3: And the chief priests were accusing Him of many things.
verses.15:4: Then Pilate questioned Him again, saying, "Do You answer nothing? Look how many things they are accusing You of."
verses.15:5: Yet Jesus answered nothing further, so that Pilate was amazed.
verses.15:6: Now at the feast he used to release to them one prisoner, whomever they requested.
verses.15:7: And the man called Barabbas had been bound with the insurrectionists who had committed murder in the insurrection.
verses.15:8: And going up, the crowd began to ask him to do just as he used to do for them.
